content:
emma_support: FYI - Acme reports their nightly canary deploys started failing right after we rotated their pipeline service account key last night. They see 403s from the Redwood API and are blocked.

emma_support: Customer pasted a curl failure: 
```
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/deploys/trigger
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"permission_denied","message":"token scope insufficient: missing 'deploy:write'"}
```

emma_support: They say the CI runner caches tokens for the pipeline-bot and didn't pick up the new key. Can eng take a look? @raj_eng @luis_sre

raj_eng: Thanks, looking. Which SA did we rotate? service account name?

emma_support: acme-pipeline@acme-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com (customer provided). Rotation was done via our console around 02:15 UTC.

luis_sre: Got it. Pinging logs. deploy-bot posted a failed webhook too earlier: 
```
[deploy-bot] 2024-07-30T02:17:12Z deploy failed job=canary-run id=job-9f3a reason=auth_error code=403
```

luis_sre: Two quick checks: 1) Is the CI still using the old private key file (json) or an ephemeral OIDC token? 2) Are we seeing token binding/malformed scopes?

emma_support: Customer said they use an in-house runner that fetches a short-lived token from our token service using the SA key. They rotate keys nightly and assume runner re-fetches.

raj_eng: Ok replicate steps: if runner still holds an access token generated before rotation, it should be invalidated when we revoke the private key. However, with service-account keys and our token-service there is a nuance: if the token was minted with limited scopes and we tightened scopes in the policy during rotation, old tokens may lack new required scopes.

dana_sec: Quick note: we recently changed the recommended minimal scope for deploys to `deploy:write` + `model:invoke`. If the rotation process replaced the SA IAM policy to be stricter but the CI minted tokens earlier with different claims, that mismatch causes permission_denied.

luis_sre: Can the customer share the actual error payload with request id? We need the request-id to correlate in logs.

emma_support: They gave this request id: req_0b7d2e4a. Pasting truncated debug from their runner: 
```
2024-07-30T02:16:59Z fetch-token: got_access_token=ya29.a0AfH6SM... expires_in=3599 scopes=openid email deploy:read
2024-07-30T02:17:11Z deploy: POST /v1/deploys/trigger headers.Authorization=Bearer ya29... response=403
```

raj_eng: Aha - token scopes only include deploy:read, not deploy:write. So CI is requesting too-small scope when minting. Why would that change after rotation? Two possibilities: 1) The SA key rotation process also toggled the default token scope in their runner config, or 2) our token service returned a different default scope based on the new key metadata (we tag rotated keys with token_profile=read-only for a short window).

dana_sec: We do add a "rotation quarantine" metadata on newly created keys for third-party accounts (safety measure) but it should not change scopes returned by the token service. That policy was recently scoped to external partners only; need to confirm if acme was flagged.

luis_sre: I searched by req_0b7d2e4a in our logs: 
```
2024-07-30T02:17:11Z req_0b7d2e4a auth.token.check token_id=tok_3c2 scope=deploy:read -> denied required=deploy:write
```

luis_sre: So the request reached our auth layer and failed scope check. Fix path: update the runner to request deploy:write, or adjust SA binding to include deploy:write for that key. But we need to decide safe remediation for customer.

emma_support: Customer is asking for an immediate unblock. They can update runner config but it's a manual deploy across many agents. Any safer hotfix?

raj_eng: Temporary option: grant the SA a broader role that maps deploy:read -> deploy:write (not ideal for least privilege). Better: rotate the key again without the "quarantine" flag so token-service returns normal scopes, or instruct them to restart runners so tokens are re-fetched with correct scope.

dana_sec: From security POV we prefer rotation-without-quarantine for customer-self-managed SAs only if they confirm they've got their secrets handled. But as a short lived mitigation we can create an interim token with deploy:write limited TTL and advise to replace in CI (ephemeral).

luis_sre: I can issue an admin-scoped ephemeral token for them for immediate unblocking. Steps: generate admin token scoped to deploy:write with TTL=1h, customer drops it into CI secrets store, restarts runners. Then plan coordinated key rotation + runner config update.

emma_support: Customer accepted that approach. They asked for clear repro and postmortem steps so they can fix pipelines long-term.

raj_eng: I'll write reproducible steps for their engineers: 
1) Confirm how the runner fetches tokens (private key JSON vs OIDC).
2) If using private key JSON, ensure runner requests proper scopes: modify OAuth2 token exchange step to include scope \"deploy:write model:invoke openid email\".
3) If using OIDC/OAuth, ensure mapping rule in our token-service allows the provider to request deploy:write.
4) After key rotation, restart runner processes to force new token mint.

raj_eng: Example commands we used to validate on our side: 
```
# simulate token mint with gcloud-like tooling
curl -X POST https://token-service.internal/token \
  -d 'grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer' \
  -d 'scope=deploy:write model:invoke openid email' \
  --cert acme-pipeline-key.json
```

raj_eng: Output we expect: 
```
{"access_token":"ya29.xxxxx","expires_in":3600,"scope":"deploy:write model:invoke openid email"}
```

dana_sec: For least-privilege guidance: don't give the pipeline SA broad org-level roles. Create a fine-grained role granting only these RPCs: redwood.deploys.create, redwood.deploys.update, redwood.models.invoke. Use role binding on the service account limited to the pipeline project.

luis_sre: Follow-up actions we've agreed: 
- I will generate the 1h emergency token and DM the customer with instructions (actioned). :white_check_mark:
- Raj will draft CI config snippets and a short how-to for rotation-safe token fetching (ETA 2h). :hourglass_flowing_sand:
- Dana will audit rotation quarantine rules to see why acme key got flagged (ETA 6h). :mag:

emma_support: Customer said emergency token worked and canary passed. They're planning a controlled rotation next maintenance window using our doc. They also asked us to add a retry/clear-cache step in our rotation docs to avoid runner-cached tokens.

raj_eng: I'll add a note in docs + a CLI helper snippet to invalidate cached tokens on runners: 
```
# helper: force the runner to fetch a new token
pkill -f pipeline-runner || true
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/internal/invalidate-token-cache -H "Authorization: Bearer <admin>" -d '{"sa":"acme-pipeline@acme-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com"}'
```

dana_sec: Added: also including a recommended post-rotation checklist: confirm runner restart, verify minted token scopes, rotate keys in a canary subset first.

luis_sre: Logging note: I'm flagging req_0b7d2e4a for postmortem sampling to ensure no other customers impacted.

emma_support: Closing loop with customer now. Thanks team. :pray:

deploy-bot: [system] Created incident INC-20240730-72 (severity=low) for auth:scope-mismatch - linked to thread 1719854321
